guidance: Brunswick, GA winters are mild and coastal -- expect brief cold snaps rather than hard freezes. White Dutch Clover goes semi-dormant but typically stays green through winter here (unlike harder-freeze zones where it browns out). Warm-season lawn grasses (centipede, bahia) go dormant and brown; do not fertilize dormant turf. In north-facing shade beds, Subterranean Clover is the winter half of the vetch-to-subclover rotation, forming a dense low mat through the cold months. Late winter (just before new spring growth starts) is the pruning window for Texas Sage / Barometer Bush (Leucophyllum frutescens) -- remove no more than one-third of the plant, and avoid pruning again once it starts blooming. Otherwise treat winter as a planning/prep season: order seed for spring cover crops and overseeding, and hold off on soil drenches/foliar feeds until active growth resumes.
